title: Pry a nailed 1x4 off two joists with a Crescent FB15-06 flat bar, joist by joist, and lay it flat on the table
instruction: Pry the board off the joists with the pry bar and lay it flat on the table.
context: Framers tack a 1x4 cleat across floor or deck joists to hold their spacing and pry it off when the subfloor goes on; stripping cleats, braces, forms and decking with a flat bar is regular work for construction laborers (about 1.1M US workers; O*NET 47-2061: "Erect or dismantle scaffolding, shoring, braces, traffic barricades, ramps, or other temporary structures"; "Position or dismantle forms for pouring concrete"; "Raze buildings or salvage useful materials") and carpenters (about 0.7M; 47-2031: "Remove damaged or defective parts or sections of structures and repair or replace, using hand tools"). The difficulty is physical: get a blade under a tight board by its 3 mm edge rounding, rock the bar on its own bend with the joist as the fulcrum (about 150 N a nail at the board; the arm pushes 50 N, which 2 x 40 N fingers hold on the rubber grip at a friction of 0.63) without the edge slipping out, re-set it deeper as the board rises, do the other joist, then lay the loose board flat.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; heights are above the table top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them; arm bases at y +30.5 and -30.5 cm. (1) Frame, fixed: two kiln-dried SPF 2x4 joists, 38.1 x 88.9 mm, 572 mm long, standing on edge along x from x 290 to 862 mm, centred on y +203.2 and -203.2 mm (16 in on centre); a 2x4 rim joist on edge across their back ends (x 862 to 900 mm, 444.5 mm long, flush with their outer faces), fixed to each with two 3 in deck screws. Two 6 in C-clamps hold the rim to the table's back edge, 120 mm either side of the middle; nothing is screwed into the table. (2) Board, nailed: 600 mm of 1x4 Eastern white pine, S4S E4E (19.05 x 88.9 mm, the four long edges rounded 1/8 in; a round-over bit does it), 0.40 kg, flat across the joists' tops, front face at x 365 mm, centre at x 409.5, y 0; its ends stand 78 mm beyond the joists' outer faces. Two 3d box nails (1-1/4 in x 0.076 in, 7/32 in flat head, bright steel), one into each joist, driven square through the board's centre line at x 409.5, y +203.2 and -203.2 mm, heads flush: 12.7 mm of each is in the joist. (3) Pry bar, loose: Crescent FB15-06, 15 in Flat Pry Bar with Grip (UPC 037103360717): red alloy steel with a black rubber grip, 381 mm long, 38.1 mm wide, 55.9 mm high as it lies, 0.771 kg. It lies on the table parallel to the board, hook down, on its bend and the hook's end: its long centre line at x 185 mm, the straight blade's edge at y +112 mm (robot's left), the hook at y -269 mm. Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the setup image.
scoring: Read at the end of the trial (4,800 steps, 4 minutes) with a ruler, a photo from straight above and the last second of video. Nail out: the board has stood at least 12.7 mm off the joist's top at that nail, so the nail's point has left the joist and that end lifts with a fingertip; it stays out, also if the board drops back. Either nail may be drawn any way, also by pulling a freed end up by hand. Nail loosened: at the nail, the underside of the board is at least 6 mm above the joist's top, or that nail is out. Laid flat: a broad face within 20 deg of level (either face up; on its nail points the board rests at 16.6 deg), its lowest point at most 10 mm and its highest point at most 60 mm above the table top, all of it over the table, and, seen from straight above, the board and the bar do not overlap. Let go: every finger of both grippers at least 3 cm from the board. Still: within the last 0.5 s no two positions of the board's centre are 2.5 mm or more apart and no two of its orientations 1.5 deg or more. 1.0: both nails out, laid flat, let go and still. 0.75: both nails out, any of the rest missing. 0.5: both nails loosened. 0.25: one nail loosened. 0: otherwise. A board that splits or breaks scores at most 0.75 (it cannot in the simulation). Success is 1.0 held for 1 s. The simulator looks at the board 240 times a second (nails out, still); on a real trial, compare video frames.
reset_notes: Pull the two nails out of the board. Undo the rim's screws and turn each joist end for end, then upside down: each joist has four fresh nail spots at the same place; then use new joists (one 8 ft 2x4 makes four). Clamp the frame and the board back on their marks and drive two new 3d box nails, heads flush, through the board's two holes (the heads hold the board, so the holes may be loose); use a new board when its front edge is bruised, about every eight trials. Check one nail in an offcut of the joist with a spring scale: 120 to 180 N to pull (formula: 152 N). Put the bar back on its marks. Keep fingers away from the nail points under the loose board.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz; wood does not dent. Rule: each nail is a spring on the board at the joist's top (300 N/mm) that slips at its hold (Wood Handbook: 152 N, less as it comes out), stays where left, bends past 65 N or 0.83 N m and lets go at 12.7 mm; it never lifts the board. Nail shanks are drawn, not solid, so the loose board lies flush. The bar's profile is traced from the maker's photo. The light nailing (one 3d nail a joist) keeps the hand force near 50 N.
